abstract: Audits deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability
system_message:
You are the Marine survey superintendent (MSS), responsible for auditing deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability across proposed subsea salvage expedition plans.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Bathymetric mapping calibration（BATHO）
information_points.content:
MSS-BATHO-865：For the Pelagic Deep Crane Derrick Expedition, acoustic calibration records document a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 50 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.
MSS-BATHO-G0C：For the Dynamic Positioning Modular Vessel Expedition, the acoustic survey calibration sheet reflects a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 25 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.
MSS-BATHO-IH0：For the Autonomous Multi-Catamaran Acoustic Expedition, acoustic survey calibration logs indicate a multibeam sonar resolution grid of 100 cm across the target shipwreck seabed footprint.

information_points.title: Audits deep-water hull integrity surveys and subsea positioning telemetry stability（SURV）
information_points.content:
MSS-SURV-XZT：For the Pelagic Deep Crane Derrick Expedition, the classification society survey report confirms that deep-water hull structural survey clearance is true based on ultrasonic non-destructive testing of the main salvage surface vessel hull. The avionics and navigation integration log confirms that acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is true with verified transponder lock, and hydrodynamic trials report a maximum seabed tether deployment drift of 1.4 m under 2.5-knot seabed cross-currents.
MSS-SURV-5D3：For the Dynamic Positioning Modular Vessel Expedition, deep-water hull structural survey clearance is true following ultrasonic non-destructive testing of the main vessel hull. Acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is true with verified lock on the transponder link, and hydrodynamic trials record a maximum seabed tether deployment drift of 1.4 m under 2.5-knot seabed cross-currents.
MSS-SURV-L7A：For the Autonomous Multi-Catamaran Acoustic Expedition, the classification society survey report confirms deep-water hull structural survey clearance is true for the main surface vessel hull. Acoustic dynamic positioning telemetry active is verified as true via the transponder telemetry link, while the maximum seabed tether deployment drift is measured at 2.5 m under 2.5-knot seabed cross-currents.
